metadata.note: Marquette, Houghton and Ontonagon Railroad (formed 1872 by consolidating the Marquette & Ontonagon and the Houghton & Ontonagon; leased in perpetuity to the Duluth, South Shore and Atlantic in 1887, purchased 1890) west of Ishpeming, Michigan Upper Peninsula: the main line Ishpeming - Champion - L'Anse and the Republic Branch, plus the predecessor Marquette and Ontonagon's passenger service Ishpeming - Champion 1867-1872. Marquette - Ishpeming is NOT redrawn here: it is the existing mho-marquette-negaunee-ishpeming feature in dssa_upper_peninsula.geojson (whose 1857-1890 span and shared DSS&A colour the research report lists as defects for a separate fix). Research report: research/branches/marquette_houghton_and_ontonagon_railroad.txt.
metadata.operator_split: Ishpeming - Champion: Marquette and Ontonagon 1867-1872 / MH&O 1872-1887, two features on identical geometry sharing the boundary year 1872 (convention of utica_black_river_railroad.geojson). The MH&O -> DSS&A split at the 1887 lease ends every MH&O feature here; the DSS&A's 1887-1890 years on this rail are left to the DSS&A layer's fix.
omitted: L'Anse - Houghton (block [4]): no passenger evidence under the MH&O for 1883-1886 -- a withheld unknown, not a known absence.
Champion - south shore of Lake Michigamme, M&O 1865-1872 (block [7]): no passenger evidence; abandoned 1872.
Marquette & Western, Marquette - Ishpeming (block [8]): no confirmed passenger year under the M&W or MH&O; NOT a freight-only exclusion.
Teal Lake Branch and mine/dock spurs (block [9]): freight only (Rule 1).
Iron Mountain Railroad 1855-1857 (block [P1]): mule-hauled (Rule 5), no passenger evidence 1857-1858.

Bay de Noquet & Marquette 1860-1865 and M&O Marquette - Ishpeming 1867-1872 (blocks [P2], [P3]): overlap the existing mho-marquette-negaunee-ishpeming feature's years; left to the separate fix of that feature.
Houghton & Ontonagon and Houghton & L'Anse (blocks [P4], [P5]): never ran trains in their own names.

not_yet_sourced: L'Anse - Houghton, 1883-1887 (report block [4]): the rail was complete in July 1883 and consolidated into the MH&O, but no passenger timetable or newspaper item for 1883-1886 was found, so it is NOT drawn under the MH&O. The DSS&A's 1887 Houghton Express is the first dated passenger evidence. Best next sources: April 1884 Official Guide MH&O table; Portage Lake Mining Gazette 1883-84.

Champion - L'Anse opening year CONFLICTS: completed Sept-Dec 1872 (DuLong chronology); 'finished on December 31, 1872' (MSU digital-repository snippet, not opened); 'in 1873' (american-rails). Drawn from 1873, which rests on the MH&O's L'Anse depot of 1873 (michiganrailroads); the first cited passenger timetable is the 1875 Official Guide (Fowler), so 1873-1874 is inference.

Republic Branch start: drawn from 1872 on michiganrailroads' statement that it opened (Republic reached Sept 1872) with passenger shuttles; first DATED passenger sighting is 1875 (Fowler, 1875 Official Guide).
MH&O consolidation day: 25 May 1872 board agreement (michiganrailroads MH&O page) vs September 1872 (MSU snippet); the year is solid, so the M&O/MH&O split year 1872 is unaffected.

Lease to the DSS&A: 15 Apr 1887 (DuLong) vs 15 Feb 1887 (american-rails; also the existing dssa_upper_peninsula feature's note). Map year 1887 either way. The DSS&A's own 1887-1890 years on Ishpeming - L'Anse are undrawn by any layer (dssa_upper_peninsula draws the DSS&A only from 1890) -- a separate fix.

Who ran the 1867-1871 passenger trains: michiganrailroads names the M&O in 1867 and 1870, but the BdN&M owned Marquette - Ishpeming until the Aug 1871 stock exchange. West of Ishpeming (the only part drawn here for the M&O) the rail was the M&O's own from 1865.
Headways and speeds throughout are estimates (Rule 3): the only frequency in the research is two passenger round trips a day Marquette - Champion (1867, 1870).

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 15.8 mi against 15.8 mi documented (Fowler: Ishpeming MP 248.5 - Champion 232.7) and 16.1 mi by michiganrailroads mileposts (169.6 - 185.7). Made of: Ishpeming - Winthrop Junction 1.6 mi on present-day untagged track; Winthrop Junction - Champion 14.2 mi on DSS&A-tagged grade/track. No straight-line legs. Waypoint fit: Ishpeming 0.2 km, Clarksburg 0.2 km, Humboldt 0.0 km, Champion 0.1 km; Greenwood 1.6 km (the OSM hamlet point lies north of the grade; the station site was not located). The east end starts 0.2 km from the end of the existing mho-marquette-negaunee-ishpeming feature (dssa_upper_peninsula.geojson). LATER-ALIGNMENT NOTES (Rule 2): the drawn line is the DSS&A/Soo-era grade (abandoned east of Humboldt, live CN west of it). It was NOT checked against the 1860s-1880s alignment. In particular the Ishpeming - Winthrop Junction 1.6 mi follows present-day track through a mining district (Lake Angeline, Cleveland, Salisbury) reshaped repeatedly after the 1860s, and the 1870 Official Guide's Ontonagon Junction was not located on it; treat the first ~2 mi as a later alignment than this feature's era. ERA NOTE: for 1867-1872 the M&O's line ran on beyond Champion along the SOUTH shore of Lake Michigamme (abandoned 1872); that is west of Champion and not drawn here (report blocks [7], UNRESOLVED 8c). Only the Ishpeming - Champion part of the M&O's Marquette - Champion run is drawn; Marquette - Ishpeming is the existing mho-marquette-negaunee-ishpeming feature.

segments.note: Marquette and Ontonagon Railroad, built west from Ontonagon Junction near Ishpeming from 1865 to Champion and Lake Michigamme. Passenger trains confirmed 1867: 'The M&O operates eleven scheduled ore trains a day in addition to two passenger trains' on 'the 32-mile run from Champion to Marquette'; in 1870 'two round trip passenger trains between Marquette and Champion', connecting at Negaunee with the Peninsula Railroad (C&NW) for Escanaba (michiganrailroads Main Line Central timeline). 1870 Official Guide station names on this stretch: Ontonagon Junction, Lake Angeline, Cleveland, Washington (Fowler). The 1865-1867 bracket is collapsed to 1867, the first confirmed passenger year. Ends 1872 on consolidation with the Houghton & Ontonagon as the Marquette, Houghton and Ontonagon (25 May vs Sept 1872 - day in conflict, year solid); the MH&O feature on this geometry starts the same year. Headway 480 min is an estimate from the two daily round trips; unsourced as an interval.
sources: Segment-level: start 1867 and the two daily passenger trains from michiganrailroads' DSS&A Main Line Central timeline (1867, 1870); end 1872 from the MH&O consolidation (michiganrailroads MH&O page). Read by the 2026-11-02 research report; secondary sources, no primary timetable seen.

properties.line: Marquette, Houghton and Ontonagon: Champion – L'Anse
properties.speed_source: estimated: 1860s-80s single-track iron-range steam road with mine traffic; no running times were read (the 1860 BdN&M figure of 1 h 45 min for 18 mi, ~16 km/h, is the only timing in the research and is for the Marquette end). Unsourced.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-11-02), routed with opstrace.py: Champion - Michigamme - Nestoria - Summit - Herman - L'Anse entirely on the live CN L'Anse Subdivision (old_railway_operator=DSS&A), 31.8 of 32.1 mi on DSS&A-tagged track, 0.4 mi untagged in yard/junction trackage. OpenHistoricalMap way -199263138 ("Duluth, South Shore and Atlantic Railroad", Champion - Baraga) and OSM abandoned/rail-trail ways over Nestoria - L'Anse were fetched to look for the pre-1883 grade; the OHM way coincides with the CN track throughout (no point more than 150 m off), and no other grade toward Taylor or L'Anse (1st) was found in either database.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 32.1 mi against ~31.3 mi documented by the later alignment (Fowler: Champion 232.7 - Nestoria 218.4 = 14.3 mi; Nestoria 48.6 - L'Anse (2nd) 31.6 from Houghton = 17.0 mi). By leg: Champion - Nestoria traced 15.5 mi vs 14.3 (8% long; possibly a later realignment along Lake Michigamme or Fowler's rounding, not resolved); Nestoria - L'Anse traced 16.6 mi vs 17.0. No straight-line legs. Waypoint fit: Champion 0.1 km, Michigamme 0.3 km, Nestoria 0.1 km, Summit 0.0 km, Herman 0.0 km, L'Anse 0.2 km. West of Champion the line runs on the NORTH shore of Lake Michigamme through Michigamme village, the 1872 MH&O alignment the report calls for (the M&O's 1865 south-shore line is not drawn). Spurr, Sturgeon, Palmer and Taylor (Junction) are not in OSM and were not used as waypoints. LATER-ALIGNMENT FLAG (Rule 2): Nestoria - L'Anse, ~17 mi, is drawn on the POST-1883 DSS&A/Soo/CN alignment via Summit and Herman to L'Anse (2nd). For 1873-1883 the line instead ran via Sturgeon, Palmer and Taylor Junction to L'Anse (1st) (Fowler table 2: Sturgeon 47, Palmer 39, Taylor Jct 37, L'Anse (1st) 32 mi from Houghton, the station 'rl. 1883'); that grade was not found in OSM, OpenHistoricalMap or any rail-trail, so for 1873-1883 this stretch -- above all the final few miles from about Herman down to the bay -- shows a later alignment than the era's. Its mileage is close to the later line's (~16.6 vs 17.0 mi), so the two probably share much of their length, but that is not shown.

segments.note: MH&O extension from Champion to L'Anse on Keweenaw Bay, built by the Houghton & Ontonagon construction company and completed at or after the 1872 consolidation (Sept-Dec 1872 per DuLong; 31 Dec 1872 per an MSU text snippet; 1873 per american-rails - conflict). Runs on the NORTH shore of Lake Michigamme through Michigamme village (built 1872, replacing the M&O's south-shore line), then Spurr, the Nestoria site, Sturgeon, Palmer and Taylor (Junction) to the original L'Anse station. Drawn from 1873, when the MH&O had a depot, merchandise dock and warehouse at L'Anse and opened its ore dock (michiganrailroads); the first cited passenger timetable is the 1875 Official Guide, in which Fowler letters L'Anse (1st), Taylor, Palmer, Sturgeon and Michigamme 'y', and the 1875 Michigan Gazetteer calls L'Anse 'the western terminus of the Marquette, Houghton & Ontonagon R. R.', with a daily boat on to Houghton. So 1873-1874 rests on the depot, not a timetable. In 1883 the line was extended to Houghton and L'Anse station relocated (L'Anse (2nd)); L'Anse - Houghton is NOT drawn (no MH&O passenger evidence 1883-1886). Ends 1887 on the DSS&A lease (15 Apr vs 15 Feb 1887). Headway 720 min is an estimate (one or two trains a day assumed; no frequency for this section was found).
sources: Segment-level: start 1873 from the MH&O's 1873 L'Anse depot (michiganrailroads L'Anse page) with service confirmed by the 1875 Official Guide letters in Fowler and the 1875 Michigan Gazetteer; end 1887 from the DSS&A lease (DuLong; american-rails). The 1873 start is an inference from a depot, not a timetable; the headway is not sourced. Read by the 2026-11-02 research report.

segments.note: Republic Branch, Humboldt - Washington Mine - Midway - Republic, 8.5 mi. Begun Oct 1871; 'Republic was reached in September, 1872', and 'Passenger service was provided by the M&O using short trains to connect with the main line' (michiganrailroads Republic Branch). Opened in the consolidation year, so drawn wholly as MH&O (report block [P6]). First DATED passenger sighting is the 1875 Official Guide (Fowler: Republic 'ya'); Midway appears in Appleton's Guide 1882. Ends 1887 as an MH&O year on the DSS&A lease; service continued under the DSS&A (June 1888 timetable train at Republic 4:12 pm; 1889 'noon train'), but those years are outside this layer and the DSS&A's end on the branch is unknown - the branch was lifted in 1928, an abandonment year, not a passenger end. Headway 480 min is an estimate (shuttles connecting with the two main-line round trips); unsourced.
